newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-AWB assessing frost effect on Australia wheat.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-AWB assessing frost effect on Australia wheat.

text.p: The Australian Wheat Board (AWB) said on Monday it was assessing whether a snap weekend frost in the farming belt of north-western New South Wales (NSW) would affect the big wheat crop in the state.
Leigh Martin, crop forecaster at the AWB, told Reuters the board's Moree office reported that it was unclear at this stage wherther there would be any effect on the crop.
"It's nothing unusual, its the sort of event they expect at this time of year," Martin said.
"They're not anticipating any substantial change to the crop at this stage," Martin said. "But it will take a couple of days to determine the effect of it," he added.
Temperatures plunged to just below freezing in the region on Friday.
New South Wales produces about a third of Australia's wheat crop, expected to be up to about 20 million tonnes this year.
